fields.features_heading: What the Form Asks Before an Agent Quotes
fields.features_subheading: Six pieces gather the home's details and its existing coverage, then put each request in front of the agent who will quote it.
fields.feature_1:
Questions about the house itself

Ask for the address, the year built, the square footage, and the roof's age. Each answer lands in its own field, so an agent can start quoting without calling the homeowner back.
fields.feature_2:
The current policy, read from one upload

Let the homeowner upload the declarations page of the current policy. The app reads the insurer, the dwelling limit, and the renewal date, and an agent checks what it cannot read.
fields.feature_3:
Requests routed by the age of the home

Set a year-built line, such as 1960, and send every older home to the agent who handles them. Newer homes go to the shared quoting queue, and each agent hears by email or Slack.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders before the renewal date

Pick how many days before renewal a request should have its quote, such as 45. When an open request crosses that line with no quote sent, the app emails the agent who owns it.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen on a phone

Offer the form one question at a time, so it reads well on a phone. An early answer about the kind of home hides questions that do not apply, like the roof's age for a condo unit.
fields.feature_6:
Requests kept in a database you own

Every request saves to a database you own, with no response caps. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep building on it with your own developer.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Agencies Take Quote Requests
fields.tab_content_1:
A 1998 house arrives with its roof age and renewal date

Lisbeth Arnaud's policy renews April 14, and she is collecting quotes first. On her phone, she fills out the Haddon Ridge Insurance form for her 2,350-square-foot house, built in 1998 with a 7-year-old roof. Agent Rhys Marsden gets the request by email, every answer in its own field, and starts quoting that afternoon.
fields.tab_content_2:
Homes built before 1960 go to the senior agent

Tollgate Insurance sends any home built before 1960 to its senior agent, Agathe Quayle, in a Slack direct message. This morning the rule caught a 1924 house at 41 Kettering Lane. The 4 newer homes from the same morning stay in the shared quoting queue, where the next free agent picks each one up.
fields.tab_content_3:
One upload answers 3 policy questions for Desmond

Desmond Pryce wants prices before his Saddlebrook Mutual policy renews on June 2. He uploads its declarations page to the Stonecrop Insurance form. The insurer, the $412,000 dwelling limit, and the June 2 renewal date fill in from the page. The deductible did not come through, and agent Imelda Corsi confirms it.
fields.tab_content_4:
Renewal is 38 days out, and a reminder reaches her agent

Brightmarsh Insurance lists 4 open quote requests on its agent dashboard by renewal date. Wilhelmina Strand's policy renews in 38 days, and no quote has gone out. Any open request within 45 days of renewal with no quote gets a reminder, here an email to her agent, Corentin Bale. The 3 renewing later get none.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Home Insurance Quote Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a home insurance quote form, build it with Emergent, and test that each request reaches its agent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Look back at last year's requests
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Offer the upload as the fast path
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Pick the agent for each home
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull 20 quote requests from last year and mark every detail an agent had to call the homeowner back for. Those details belong on the form. A question no agent used in any of the 20 can come off it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for the address and the kind of home first, then the details of the house itself. Word each question the way a homeowner talks. Nobody filling it out should have to look up a term like dwelling before answering.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Put the declarations page upload before the typed policy questions. A homeowner with the page at hand skips the typing, and one without it fills in the insurer and the renewal date by hand instead.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write down your routing rules before you build: a year-built line for older homes, a shared queue for the rest, and whether alerts go by email or Slack. Name a backup agent for days the usual one is out.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the questions, the upload, and the routing rules into one prompt. Emergent builds the form, the database behind it, and a dashboard for your agents. Change a question later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose how many days before renewal counts as too close for a request with no quote, then write that number into the prompt. Sort the agent dashboard by renewal date. The requests nearest the line sit at the top, where agents see them first.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Fill out the form on a phone
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit a test request from a phone for a made-up 1950 house with a sample declarations page. Check that it reaches the senior agent, that the upload filled the right fields, and that the request sits in the table.

faq_plan.q: What is a home insurance quote form?
faq_plan.a: A home insurance quote form is the online form a homeowner fills out to ask an agency for a homeowners policy price. It collects the address, the details of the house, and the current policy if there is one. An agent can then prepare a quote without a phone interview first.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a home insurance quote form?
faq_plan.a: List what to ask about the home and its coverage, then decide which agent gets each request. Describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. The result is a working form, with every request saved and an agent view of what is still open.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a home insurance quote form ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the homeowner's name, email, and phone first. Then cover the address, the kind of home, when it was built, its square footage, and how old the roof is. Finish with the current insurer and the renewal date, or an upload of the declarations page. Leave coverage choices for the agent to talk through on the call.

faq_plan.q: How is a home insurance quote form different from one for a repair job?
faq_plan.a: It describes a house and a policy instead of a job. A construction quote form lays out work to be done, such as a new deck, and the contractor prices the labor and materials. A home insurance request records the house as it stands and the coverage it carries now. The agent prices a policy from that.

faq_plan.q: Can a home insurance quote form read the current policy from an upload?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A declarations page itemizes the coverages and their limits of liability. It also lists the dates coverage begins and ends, and one upload can replace several typed answers. Ask for a clear photo or the insurer's own file. Emergent can build that upload step, and the app reads the values into fields, leaving unclear ones for an agent.

faq_plan.q: How should a home insurance quote form route requests to agents?
faq_plan.a: By a rule that fits in one line. Route on the year built, the ZIP code in the address, or the kind of home, and send everything else to a shared queue. Each agent gets an email or a Slack message with a link to the full request, and a backup agent covers days off.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a home insurance quote form have?
faq_plan.a: About 10: the questions an agent needs for a first quote. A cleaning quote form can price a home from its rooms alone, while an insurance request also needs the year built, the roof's age, and the current policy. Showing one question per screen keeps that length manageable on a phone.

faq_plan.q: What should a homeowner get back after submitting a home insurance quote form?
faq_plan.a: A confirmation email that names the agent handling the request and says when to expect a quote. Send it the moment the form is submitted, with a copy of the answers attached. A homeowner who spots a wrong year built or address can then reply before the agent starts quoting.

faq_plan.q: Can a home insurance quote form handle condos and rental homes?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask the kind of home on the first screen, then show only the questions that fit it. A condo unit skips the roof's age, and a rental home can go straight to the agent who quotes rentals. Every answer, whichever path it took, lands in the same database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can one home insurance quote form collect details for several carriers at once?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The homeowner answers once, and agents use that one request to quote with each carrier they work with. The pattern matches the rfq form: one description of the need gathers prices from several sources. Emergent builds the form from a plain-English prompt, and the free tier covers building and publishing.

plan.angle: Wave 3 page with no top 10 in the workbook, and every AlsoAsked question is a shopper's question about prices and carriers, so the page wins on depth for the agency building the form: questions that change with the kind of home, the current policy read in from its declarations page, routing by the home's age to the agent who places older homes, and a reminder before the homeowner's current policy renews. Four agencies an agent will recognize: a homeowner shopping before renewal, a 1924 house sent to the senior agent, a switch from another carrier started from a declarations page, and requests that sit too close to renewal. The FAQ defines the form and how to build one, then answers what an agency setting one up asks: what to ask about the house, keeping quote requests in their own inbox, reading the current policy, routing, what to send back, photos, length, and rental homes. No premiums, carrier rules or coverage advice.
